title: Rootless explicit single-ID mapping produces empty intermediate OCI root
body:
### Issue Description

Rootless Podman fails during OCI initialization when using explicit single-ID UID/GID mappings. Podman successfully mounts the container image's overlay filesystem at the normal rootless storage merged path, but the generated OCI configuration gives crun a root.path under /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>. During the observed failure, crun cannot see the image filesystem through that path.

The first observed failure is while crun tries to open /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>/etc/hosts, which returns No such file or directory. A /run/.containerenv failure can occur later, but /etc/hosts failing first indicates that this is not specific to .containerenv.

The container uses an intentionally narrow mapping:

--uidmap=65532:1:1

--gidmap=65532:1:1

--user=65532:65532

The generated OCI spec contains those same one-entry UID/GID mappings. The failure occurs during podman container init; the container workload is never started.

Environment: Kali Linux/Debian-based, amd64, rootless Podman with native overlay on ext4. Podman 5.8.3+ds1-1, crun 1.28-1, conmon 2.1.13+ds1-2.

Is this a known issue with Podman's rootless intermediate-root staging when explicit UID/GID mappings deliberately leave container UID/GID 0 unmapped? If it has already been fixed upstream, which commit and first Podman release contain the fix?

### Steps to reproduce the issue


1. On a rootless Podman installation, create an inert container using explicit single-ID mappings:

   podman create \
     --name single-id-repro \
     --network=none \
     --uidmap=65532:1:1 \
     --gidmap=65532:1:1 \
     --user=65532:65532 \
     --read-only \
     <IMAGE> \
     <INERT_COMMAND>

2. Initialize the container with runtime debug logging, but do not start it:

   podman --log-level=debug \
     --runtime-flag=debug \
     --runtime-flag=log=/tmp/crun-single-id-repro.log \
     container init single-id-repro

3. Observe that OCI initialization fails before the container workload starts. In the reproduced case, crun reports:

   open `/var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>/etc/hosts`:
   No such file or directory

4. Inspect the generated OCI config.json. It identifies:

   root.path = /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>

   while the UID/GID mappings remain:

   container UID 65532 -> host/intermediate ID 1, size 1
   container GID 65532 -> host/intermediate ID 1, size 1

5. Podman debug output shows that the image overlay was successfully mounted separately at its normal rootless storage `merged` path.

6. Do not issue `podman start`. Remove the inert reproducer afterward:

   podman rm --force --ignore single-id-repro

### Describe the results you received

podman container init fails before the container process starts.

Podman successfully mounts the populated image overlay at its normal rootless-storage merged location, but the generated OCI specification gives crun a root path under /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>.

That intermediate root does not contain the expected image filesystem. The first observed crun failure is resolving:

/var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>/etc/hosts

which returns No such file or directory.

The generated OCI configuration still contains the requested single-entry UID/GID mappings (65532 -> 1, size 1) and process identity 65532:65532.

The workload itself is never executed.

### Describe the results you expected

podman container init should successfully prepare the OCI container without starting the workload.

The OCI root.path supplied to crun should expose the populated image root filesystem, including directories such as /etc and /run, so that OCI mount targets such as /etc/hosts can be prepared successfully.

If this explicit single-ID UID/GID mapping is unsupported, Podman should instead reject the configuration with a clear mapping-related error rather than handing crun an intermediate root that does not contain the image filesystem.

### podman info output

```yaml
Podman version: 5.8.3+ds1-1
crun version: 1.28-1
conmon version: 2.1.13+ds1-2

OS: Kali Linux (Debian-based)
Architecture: amd64
Mode: rootless
Storage driver: overlay (native overlay)
Backing filesystem: ext4
OCI runtime: crun
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

Kali Linux (Debian-based), amd64. Podman is running rootless directly on the host, not inside a container. Storage uses native overlay on ext4. OCI runtime is crun. The reproducer intentionally uses explicit single-ID UID/GID mappings and leaves container UID/GID 0 unmapped.

### Additional information

The failure appears to occur at the handoff between Podman's rootless intermediate-root staging and crun.

Podman debug evidence showed the real image overlay mounted successfully at its normal .../overlay/<layer>/merged location, while the generated OCI root.path pointed to /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>. That intermediate root did not expose the expected image filesystem when crun performed OCI initialization.

The first observed failure was /etc/hosts, before /run/.containerenv, so the issue does not appear to be .containerenv-specific.

I have not worked around the problem by broadening the UID/GID mappings, mapping container root, changing host permissions, or modifying the image.

I have also not reproduced this against the latest upstream Podman release yet.

Is this a known intermediate-root staging issue? If it has already been fixed upstream, could you point me to the fixing commit and the first release containing it? I can provide sanitized OCI config.json and Podman/crun debug excerpts if useful.
